cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities where input parsing code makes unchecked assumptions about string characteristics (null-termination, quote delimiters) and integer sizes (minimum length, maximum value, non-zero record size). These assumptions lead to out-of-bounds reads, heap buffer overflows, integer underflow/overflow, and infinite loops. Fixes require adding explicit validation checks before performing memory operations or arithmetic.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata into memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work. Report code paths where protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 8 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work.

mechanism.missing_guard: protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion
mechanism.name: unbounded binary length or size field drives resource use
mechanism.sink_shape: memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Validate string length and content (e.g., check for null terminator presence, leading/trailing quotes) before using them in memory operations; use explicit lengths or bounds checks to prevent over-reads and overflows.
sub_patterns.name: Unchecked assumptions on string terminator and quote delimiters
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code assumes that parsed strings are always null-terminated, enclosed in double quotes, or have a specific minimal length without verifying these properties, causing out-of-bounds reads, heap overflows, or infinite loops when the assumption fails.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add enforce() or assert() checks to ensure integer values are within expected bounds (e.g., size >= threshold, size <= max, record size > 0) before using them in arithmetic, allocation, or loop control.
sub_patterns.name: Missing lower and upper bound checks on integer fields used in pointer arithmetic or loops
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code assumes that integer values (size, count) are within safe ranges (e.g., >= minimum, <= maximum, >0) without validation, leading to integer underflow/overflow, out-of-bounds access, or infinite loops.
